criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: Identifies overbroad MAE carve-outs for environmental industry/regulations
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies the environmental-services industry and Environmental Law/regulation carve-outs as unacceptable without a disproportionate-impact exception, and proposes language applying such a qualifier to those carve-outs.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: Proposes adding disproportionate impact qualifier to MAE carve-outs
criteria_results.reasoning: The proposed MAE definition adds a disproportionate-impact exception covering clauses (i) through (v), including the industry and Environmental Law/regulatory carve-outs, where the effects disproportionately affect the Company relative to other industry participants.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: Provides actual revised contract language for MAE definition
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum includes a full proposed replacement MAE definition as clean contract text, including a disproportionate-impact exception for clauses (i) through (v).

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: Explains rationale — environmental company needs MAE protection
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly explains that Cascadia is an environmental-services business, so unqualified industry and environmental-law carve-outs could exclude the target-specific regulatory and environmental harms most likely to affect it. It therefore justifies adding a disproportionate-impact exception to preserve meaningful MAE protection.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: Identifies missing interim covenant restricting affiliate transactions
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies that the interim covenants lack a restriction on transactions or arrangements between the Company and Seller or Seller affiliates, and proposes a new Section 6.01(b)(xiv) covering entry into, amendment, renewal, termination, payments, and asset transfers involving such parties before closing.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: Proposes covenant requiring Buyer consent for affiliate transactions
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum proposes new Section 6.01(b)(xiv), which bars the Company from entering into, amending, modifying, extending, renewing, supplementing, or terminating transactions or arrangements with Seller or Seller affiliates without Buyer's prior written consent.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: References the above-market rent to Seller affiliate as rationale
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly ties the affiliate transaction covenant to the disclosed “$1.6 million annual above-market Affiliate Lease,” explaining that the covenant is needed to prevent Seller from expanding, amending, extending, renewing, prepaying, or adding affiliate arrangements before closing.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003: Identifies indemnification cap discrepancy (20% vs. 12.5%)
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies that the Seller draft sets the general indemnification cap at 20% of the $215 million Base Enterprise Value ($43 million), while the term sheet requires 12.5% ($26.875 million), and proposes conforming both the definition and operative cap provision.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003: Proposes redline reducing cap to 12.5% / $26,875,000
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly proposes revising the Indemnification Cap to 12.5% of the $215,000,000 Base Enterprise Value, correctly stated as $26,875,000, both in Section 1.01 and the operative cap provision in Section 9.04(b).

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003: References the term sheet as basis for cap correction
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly cites the executed September 10, 2025 term sheet as a reviewed source and, in the indemnification-cap markup, states that the agreed cap is 12.5% and cites “Term Sheet §8 (General Indemnification Cap)” as the basis for correcting the seller draft’s 20% cap.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004: Identifies that environmental reps survival period is too short
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies that the seller draft gives non-fundamental representations, including environmental representations, only 12 months of survival and states that this is inadequate for environmental liabilities. It proposes a 36-month survival period for Environmental Representations, including Section 4.15 Environmental Matters covering environmental compliance and permits.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004: Proposes extending environmental reps survival to at least 36 months
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly proposes that the Environmental Representations survive for 36 months following closing and also notes a preferred full-statute-of-limitations position for CERCLA-related matters.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004: References CERCLA/Dalton Creek exposure as rationale for longer survival
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly connects Dalton Creek’s CERCLA exposure and other environmental risks to longer survival. In Issue 12, it states that environmental liabilities may take years to crystallize, proposes 36-month survival (with a preferred full-statute period for CERCLA matters), and cites Dalton Creek/CERCLA latency and active remediation as support.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005: Identifies anti-sandbagging provision in Section 9.06
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies Section 9.06 as an anti-sandbagging provision and quotes its restriction that Buyer cannot obtain indemnification for breaches or inaccuracies of which Buyer or its Representatives had Knowledge as of the Closing Date.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005: Proposes replacing with pro-sandbagging language
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 9.06 expressly replaces the seller’s anti-sandbagging provision with a pro-sandbagging clause stating that Buyer’s indemnification and other remedies are not affected, limited, diminished, or impaired by any investigation or knowledge acquired or capable of being acquired before or after execution or Closing.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005: Provides actual pro-sandbagging contract text
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum includes actual proposed pro-sandbagging contract language in Section 9.06, stating that Buyer’s indemnification and other remedies are not affected by investigations or knowledge acquired before or after signing or closing.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006: Identifies need for Special Indemnity for Dalton Creek CERCLA matter
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly proposes a separate “Dalton Creek Special Indemnity” in new Section 9.09 for the EPA CERCLA § 104(e) matter. It further provides that this indemnity is dollar-one, outside the general basket and indemnification cap, and has separate survival and escrow treatment, rather than relying solely on general environmental representations.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006: Special Indemnity survival of 72 months
criteria_results.reasoning: The proposed Dalton Creek Special Indemnity in Section 9.09(c) expressly states that it “shall survive the Closing for seventy-two (72) months,” satisfying the required six-year post-closing survival period.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006: Special Indemnity not subject to basket or cap
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly states in proposed Section 9.09(b) that the Dalton Creek Special Indemnity “shall not be subject to the Basket Amount or the Indemnification Cap” and confirms that such losses will neither reduce the cap nor be subject to the basket. Section 9.04(b) also expressly excludes Section 9.09 losses from the general cap.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006: References Dalton Creek liability range ($1.5M-$6M)
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly states that Dalton Creek has an estimated exposure of $1.5 million to $6 million and uses that range to justify the Dalton Creek Special Indemnity, including in Issue 13's commentary.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_007: Identifies problematic earnout operational covenant
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies Section 2.05(d) as an overly restrictive earnout operational covenant, quotes the requirement to operate consistently with past practice and in good faith to maximize the earnout, and proposes replacing it with a narrow primary-purpose anti-avoidance covenant.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_007: Proposes limiting earnout covenant to no-frustration standard
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly replaces the affirmative past-practice and earnout-maximization obligations with a narrow covenant prohibiting actions taken with the primary purpose of reducing or avoiding the earnout payment, while preserving Buyer's discretion to operate, integrate, and restructure the business.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_007: Explains rationale — Buyer integration/restructuring flexibility
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly explains that the seller’s broad earnout covenant would constrain Buyer’s integration, restructuring, bolt-on acquisitions, personnel decisions, and resource allocation during the earnout period, creating litigation risk over ordinary business decisions. It also proposes language preserving Buyer’s discretion to integrate, restructure, and otherwise manage the Company.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008: Identifies missing payoff letter requirement
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly notes that the Seller draft permits repayment at or promptly following closing and lacks payoff-letter timing, content, and funding mechanics. It proposes requiring payoff letters from each holder of Target Indebtedness at least three business days before closing.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008: Proposes payoff letters at least 3 business days pre-closing
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly requires executed payoff letters to be delivered no later than three Business Days before Closing, and requires each letter to include wire transfer instructions and lien-release documentation, including UCC termination statements.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008: Proposes simultaneous repayment at closing through funds flow
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly replaces the seller’s “at or promptly following Closing” language with a requirement that all Closing/Target Indebtedness be repaid, discharged, and satisfied in full simultaneously with Closing through the closing funds flow, with Buyer paying the holders directly under payoff letters and the Funds Flow Agreement.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008: Proposes payoff letter delivery as a condition to closing
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly proposes adding a Buyer closing condition in Section 7.02 requiring Seller to deliver the payoff letters at least three business days before Closing and requiring those letters to remain effective and provide for lien releases upon payment.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009: Identifies missing government contract anti-assignment/novation requirement
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies that the seller draft's generic consent provisions do not adequately address anti-assignment, novation, and recognition requirements for the Oregon DEQ, Washington Ecology, U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, and Bureau of Land Management contracts. It proposes specific representations, covenants, and closing conditions addressing the Anti-Assignment Act and FAR Part 42 novation requirements.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009: References specific government contracts requiring novation
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum specifically lists the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers and Bureau of Land Management contracts and identifies the two federal contracts as requiring focused FAR Part 42 novation/recognition analysis, satisfying the requirement to identify at least two contracts.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009: Proposes closing condition or covenant for government contract novation
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum proposes both a specific pre-closing covenant in new Section 6.06 requiring Seller and the Company to notify contracting officers and seek required novation or recognition agreements, and a closing condition in Section 7.02(h) addressing timely submissions, no adverse agency action, and interim-performance confirmation.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009: References Anti-Assignment Act or FAR provisions
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly cites both the Anti-Assignment Act, 41 U.S.C. § 6305, and FAR Part 42/Subpart 42.12 as the legal basis for federal government-contract novation and recognition requirements.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_010: Identifies missing environmental permit transfer/notification covenant
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies that the seller draft lacks a covenant addressing environmental permit change notifications and post-closing cooperation. It proposes a new Section 6.07 requiring identification and submission of required permit notifications/applications before closing and Seller cooperation after closing with permit transfer, re-issuance, amendment, notification, and approval processes.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_010: Proposes cooperation covenant for environmental permit transfers
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum proposes a new Section 6.07 requiring Seller, pre-closing, to identify permit-related change-of-control requirements and prepare and submit required notifications and applications. It also requires post-closing cooperation with permit notification, transfer, re-issuance, amendment, and approval processes, including executing documents and participating in agency communications.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_010: Notes that permits may require notification even in a stock deal
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly states that “The stock structure preserves the permit-holding entity but does not eliminate change-of-control notifications,” and proposes identifying and completing permit notifications or approvals required by issuing agencies. This directly captures the required stock-deal nuance.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_011: Identifies missing R&W Insurance subrogation waiver
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly states in Issue 16 that the Seller draft "contains no R&W Insurance provision" and proposes a new Section 9.10 requiring the R&W insurer to waive subrogation and recovery rights against Seller and related parties, except for actual fraud. It also reiterates the omission in the conclusion.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_011: Proposes subrogation waiver provision with fraud exception
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum proposes new Section 9.10 requiring the R&W Insurance Policy to waive the insurer’s subrogation and recovery rights against Seller and related persons, with an express exception for claims arising from or relating to Seller’s actual fraud.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_011: References R&W Insurance policy / Granite Ridge Underwriters
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly states that Buyer is obtaining an R&W Insurance policy from Granite Ridge Underwriters and separately proposes an R&W Insurance subrogation waiver, explaining that it protects Seller from insurer subrogation except in cases of fraud.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_012: Identifies non-compete scope exceeds term sheet (duration)
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies that the Seller draft imposes a five-year non-compete while the term sheet specifies a three-year period, and it proposes replacing the duration with three years.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_012: Identifies non-compete scope exceeds term sheet (geographic)
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies that the seller draft imposes a nationwide restriction and states that the term sheet limits the non-compete to Oregon, Washington, California, and Nevada. It also proposes replacement language reflecting those four states.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_012: Identifies non-compete scope exceeds term sheet (activity)
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies that the seller draft’s five-year nationwide restriction on engaging in “any business” is overbroad and conflicts with the term sheet, which limits the restricted activity to environmental remediation and hazardous waste management services.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_012: Proposes narrowing non-compete duration to 3 years
criteria_results.reasoning: The proposed replacement for Section 6.09(a) expressly narrows the non-compete period from five years to three years following the Closing Date, matching the term sheet.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_012: Proposes narrowing non-compete geographic scope to OR, WA, CA, NV
criteria_results.reasoning: The proposed replacement for Section 6.09(a) expressly limits the non-compete geographic scope to Oregon, Washington, California, and Nevada, matching the term sheet.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_012: Proposes narrowing non-compete activity scope to environmental remediation and hazardous waste management
criteria_results.reasoning: The proposed replacement for Section 6.09(a) expressly limits the non-compete to businesses engaged in “environmental remediation services or hazardous waste management services,” matching the term sheet’s activity scope.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_012: Notes enforceability risk of overbroad non-compete
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly states that the five-year nationwide restriction covering “any business” would sweep in Evergreen’s legitimate construction and timber operations and creates enforceability risk. It also proposes a narrower four-state, activity-specific covenant with carve-outs for those businesses.

criteria_results.title: Indemnification cap issue rated as Critical or High priority
criteria_results.reasoning: The indemnification cap discrepancy is expressly labeled [HIGH] in both the definition and operative cap discussions, satisfying the requirement that it be rated Critical or High.

criteria_results.title: Anti-sandbagging issue rated as Critical or High priority
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 9.06, addressing pro-sandbagging and deletion of the anti-sandbagging language, is expressly labeled “[CRITICAL],” the highest priority tier.

criteria_results.title: Memorandum identifies provisions acceptable as drafted
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum includes a separate “Items to Leave Unmarked” section identifying several acceptable seller-draft provisions, including the 1% true-deductible basket, limited actual-knowledge definition, good-standing certificate timing, Delaware governing law, and earnout financial mechanics. It briefly explains that these positions conform to partner instructions, the playbook, or the executed term sheet.

criteria_results.title: Memorandum flags items for partner/client discussion
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly flags multiple issues for further partner/client discussion in the “Client Decisions and Closing Checklist,” including federal novation closing conditions, environmental survival, and the Dalton Creek escrow structure. It also specifically calls for discussion with Marcus regarding government-contract and CERCLA positions.

criteria_results.title: Escrow amount correctly stated as $16,125,000 (7.5% of EV)
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum correctly states the Escrow Amount as $16,125,000, equal to 7.5% of the $215,000,000 Base Enterprise Value, and does not use an incorrect escrow figure elsewhere.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006: Proposes 36-month escrow holdback for Special Indemnity
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly provides that the escrow portion allocated to the Dalton Creek Special Indemnity remains available for 36 months after closing, distinct from the 18-month general escrow release. It also revises the escrow release provision to retain funds for Special Indemnity claims through month 36.

criteria_results.title: Earnout maximum correctly referenced as $25,000,000
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum correctly states that the earnout is up to $25,000,000 in the key deal facts and reiterates the $25 million maximum in its discussion of Section 2.05(d).

criteria_results.title: Earnout Adjusted EBITDA threshold correctly referenced as $38,000,000
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum correctly states that the earnout is paid in full at the $38,000,000 TTM Adjusted EBITDA threshold, including in the key deal facts and the earnout commentary.

criteria_results.title: Earnout floor correctly referenced as $32,000,000
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum correctly states that the earnout has a $32,000,000 floor, with no payment below that amount and linear interpolation up to the $38,000,000 full-payment threshold.

criteria_results.title: References playbook as authority for at least 3 markup positions
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum cites the Buyer M&A Playbook as authority for well over three distinct markup positions, including the MAE disproportionate-impact exception, indemnification cap, earnout covenant, debt payoff mechanics, government-contract provisions, environmental survival, Dalton Creek special indemnity, and pro-sandbagging language.

criteria_results.title: References term sheet as authority for at least 3 markup positions
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum cites the executed term sheet as authority for well over three distinct markup positions, including the indemnification cap, earnout covenant, debt payoff mechanics, government-contract protections, non-compete/non-solicit scope, survival periods, Dalton Creek special indemnity, and R&W insurance provisions.

criteria_results.title: References environmental DD memo for at least one markup position
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum repeatedly cites the environmental due diligence memorandum as support for markup positions, including the Dalton Creek special indemnity, government-contract novation, permit-transfer cooperation, and environmental representation survival provisions.

criteria_results.title: Memorandum identifies specific SPA section numbers for issues
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum ties well over 8 issues to specific SPA section numbers, including Sections 1.01, 2.05(d), 2.03(d), 2.08(a), 4.15, 4.16, 4.17, 6.01(b), 6.09, 7.02, 9.01, 9.02, 9.04(b), 9.06, and 9.08, as well as proposed new numbered sections.

criteria_results.title: Proposed redline language is actual contract text for at least 8 issues
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum provides insertion-ready proposed contract language for well over 8 issues, including MAE, indemnification cap, earnout covenant, debt payoff, government contracts, environmental representations and covenants, affiliate transactions, closing conditions, survival, Dalton Creek indemnity, sandbagging, escrow, and R&W insurance provisions.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008: Identifies all three sources of Target indebtedness
criteria_results.reasoning: The payoff-letter provision expressly identifies all three Target indebtedness sources: Cascade Mutual Bank ($28.0M senior term loan), Pacific Lease Corp. ($9.8M equipment financing), and Evergreen Holdings Group, Inc. ($4.5M subordinated seller note).
